card.summary_ko: 1882년 인천에서 조선과 미국이 맺은 14款의 수호통상조약으로, 조선이 서양 나라와 맺은 첫 조약이다. 거중조정·최혜국 대우·치외법권을 담고 있다.
card.summary_en: The 14-article treaty of amity and commerce signed at Incheon in 1882, Joseon's first treaty with a Western power; it contains good offices, most-favoured-nation treatment and extraterritoriality.
card.edition_ko: 조미수호통상조약 — 한국어 위키문헌, 판 411447; 원문은 공문서(저작권법 제7조)로 보호 대상이 아니며, 전사는 위키문헌 기여자(CC BY-SA 4.0)

notes.ko:
**저자 (체결 주체)** 조약문 서명자는 조선 측 전권대관 신헌(통리기무아문 사무를 맡은 판중추부사)과 전권부관 김홍집, 미국 측 해군 제독 로버트 슈펠트(1822–1895)이다. 교섭의 배후에는 청의 북양대신 이홍장(1823–1901)이 있었다. 이홍장은 양무운동을 이끈 관료로, 일본과 러시아를 견제하려면 조선이 서양 열강과 수교하는 것이 낫다고 보았고, 천진에서 그의 막료 마건충이 슈펠트와 초안을 논의했다. 그는 조약에 조선이 청의 속방임을 명시하려 했으나 슈펠트가 반대해 조약문에는 들어가지 않았고, 대신 조선 국왕이 별도 문서로 속방 관계를 밝혔다고 전한다. 김홍집(1842–1896)은 온건 개화파로 1880년 일본에서 《조선책략》을 가져온 인물이며, 1896년 아관파천 직후 군중에게 살해되었다. 신헌은 1876년 강화도 조약의 조선 측 대표이기도 했다.

**시대적 맥락** 1876년 개항 뒤 청은 일본과 러시아를 견제하려고 조선에 서양과의 수교를 권했다. 1881년 영남 유생들의 만인소 같은 위정척사 반대가 있었으나 정부는 교섭을 이어 갔다. 교섭은 청의 주선으로 진행되었고, 조인 두 달 뒤인 1882년 7월 임오군란이 일어났다. 이후 영국·독일(1883), 이탈리아·러시아(1884), 프랑스(1886) 등과 잇따라 조약이 맺어졌다.

**배경** 1882년 5월 22일 인천(제물포)에서 한문·영문으로 조인되고, 1883년 5월 19일 서울에서 비준서가 교환되었다. 조약문에는 조선 측이 '전권대관 경리통리기무아문사'로 적혀 있다. 이 판본은 한국어 위키문헌 「조미수호통상조약」이며, 잘못 옮겨진 글자(예: 由를 山으로, 葯을 箹로)와 빠진 부분이 있다. 특히 제5조의 세율 부분(수입 일용품·사치품의 상한)은 글이 일부 빠진 듯하다.

**의의** 조선이 서양 나라와 맺은 첫 조약이다. 제1조의 거중조정(제3국의 부당한 침해 시 서로 돕고 조정)은 뒤에 조선이 미국에 기대를 걸게 한 조항이다. 제4조의 치외법권은 조선의 법제가 정비되면 철회한다는 단서가 붙어 있다. 제5조는 관세 부과권이 조선에 있음을 밝혔고, 제7조는 아편 금지, 제14조는 최혜국 대우를 규정한다. 1883년 조선은 민영익을 전권대사로 한 보빙사를 미국에 보냈다.

**형식과 주제** 전문과 14款, 맺음말, 서명으로 이루어진 한문 조약문이다. 이 판본은 원문 句讀 없이 이어져 있어 읽기 어렵다. 주제는 우호와 조정(1), 외교관·영사(2), 난파선 구호(3), 거주민 보호와 영사 재판(4), 관세(5), 거주·통상(6), 아편(7), 곡물 금수(8), 무기(9), 교육 교류(11), 문서 언어(13), 최혜국(14)이다.

**읽기 도움**
- 伯理爾天德: 대통령(president의 음역)
- 水師總兵: 해군 제독 (슈펠트의 직함)
- 全權大官: 전권대사
- 領事: 영사
- 洋藥: 아편
- 紅蔘: 홍삼
- 最優之國: 최혜국
- 批准: 비준
- 彼此: 서로, 양쪽
- 款(관): 조항
notes.en:
**About the author (signatories)** The treaty was signed for Joseon by Shin Heon, Chief of the Privy Council Office in charge of the Office for Handling State Affairs, as plenipotentiary, and Kim Hong-jip as deputy plenipotentiary, and for the United States by Commodore Robert W. Shufeldt (1822-1895). Behind the negotiation stood the Qing viceroy Li Hongzhang (1823-1901), a leader of the Self-Strengthening Movement, who judged that Joseon would be safer opening to Western powers as a check on Japan and Russia; his aide Ma Jianzhong discussed the draft with Shufeldt at Tianjin. Li wanted the treaty to state that Joseon was a Qing dependency, but Shufeldt objected, so the clause was left out and, according to tradition, the Joseon king declared the relationship in a separate communication. Kim Hong-jip (1842-1896) was a moderate reformer who brought back Huang Zunxian's "Strategy for Korea" from Japan in 1880 and was killed by a crowd in 1896 after the king's flight to the Russian legation. Shin Heon had also been Joseon's chief negotiator at Ganghwa in 1876.

**Historical context** After the opening of ports to Japan in 1876, Qing urged Joseon to establish ties with Western states to balance Japan and Russia. Conservative scholars protested (for example the 1881 mass petition from Yeongnam), but the government continued. The negotiation was brokered by Qing, and only two months after signing the Imo Mutiny broke out in July 1882. Treaties with Britain and Germany (1883), Italy and Russia (1884) and France (1886) followed.

**Background** Signed at Incheon (Jemulpo) on 22 May 1882 in Chinese and English texts; ratifications were exchanged in Seoul on 19 May 1883. In the text, Joseon's envoys are styled "plenipotentiary in charge of the Office for Handling State Affairs". This edition is the Korean Wikisource page "조미수호통상조약", and it contains miscopied characters (e.g. 山 for 由, 箹 for 葯) and apparent gaps, notably in Article 5 where the duty-rate clauses on daily-use and luxury imports look incomplete.

**Significance** Joseon's first treaty with a Western power. Article 1 provides good offices (mutual help and mediation if a third power acts unjustly), a clause on which Joseon later placed hopes. Article 4's extraterritoriality carries a proviso that it will be withdrawn once Joseon reforms its laws. Article 5 asserts Joseon's right to set tariffs, Article 7 bans opium, and Article 14 grants most-favoured-nation treatment. In 1883 Joseon sent a mission headed by Min Yeong-ik to the United States.

**Form and themes** A Chinese-language treaty with preamble, fourteen articles, closing formula and signatures. This edition runs on without punctuation, which makes it hard going. Themes: friendship and mediation (1), diplomats and consuls (2), relief of wrecked ships (3), protection of residents and consular jurisdiction (4), tariffs (5), residence and trade (6), opium (7), grain embargo (8), arms (9), educational exchange (11), language of documents (13), most-favoured nation (14).

**Reading help**
- 伯理爾天德: "President" (transliteration)
- 水師總兵: naval commodore (Shufeldt's title)
- 全權大官: plenipotentiary
- 領事: consul
- 洋藥: opium ("foreign medicine")
- 紅蔘: red ginseng
- 最優之國: most-favoured nation
- 批准: ratification
- 彼此: each other, both sides
- 款 (gwan): article

paragraphs.orig: 朝美修好通商條約
paragraphs.en: Treaty of Amity and Commerce between Joseon and America

paragraphs.orig: 千八百八十二年 五月二十二日於仁川調印（漢, 英文）
paragraphs.en: Signed at Incheon on 22 May 1882 (Chinese and English texts)

paragraphs.orig: 千八百八十三年 五月十九日於京城批准書交換
paragraphs.en: Ratifications exchanged at the capital on 19 May 1883

paragraphs.orig: 大朝鮮國與大亞美理駕合衆國切欲敦崇和好惠顧彼此人民是以大朝鮮國君主特派全權大官經理統理機務衙門事申櫶全權副經理統理機務衙門事金弘集大美國伯理爾天德特派全權大臣水師總兵薛斐爾各將所奉全權字據互相較閱俱屬妥善訂立條臚列於左
paragraphs.en: Great Joseon and the Great United States of America, earnestly desiring to promote and cherish harmony and goodwill toward each other's peoples, the sovereign of Great Joseon has specially dispatched as plenipotentiary Shin Heon, Senior Official in charge of the Office for Handling State Affairs, with Kim Hong-jip, Deputy Plenipotentiary in charge of the Office for Handling State Affairs; and the President of the Great United States has specially dispatched as plenipotentiary Shufeldt, Commodore of the Navy. Each has exchanged and compared the full powers he bears, and finding them all in good order, they have drawn up and set out the articles below.

paragraphs.orig: 第一款嗣後大朝鮮國君主大美國伯理爾天德並其商民各皆永遠和平友好若他國有何不公輕藐之事一經照知必須相助從中善爲調處以示友誼關切
paragraphs.en: Article 1. From now on the sovereign of Great Joseon and the President of the Great United States, and their merchants and people, shall be at peace and in friendship forever. If another country should act unjustly toward or slight either of them, once notified they shall assist each other and use their good offices in mediation, to show their friendly concern.

paragraphs.orig: 第二款此次立約通商和好從兩國可交派秉權大臣駐紮彼此都城並於彼此通商口岸設立領事等官均聽其便此等官員與本地方官交涉往來均應用品級相當之禮兩國秉權大臣與領事等官享獲種種恩施與彼此所待最優之國官員無異惟領事官必須奉到駐紮之國批准文憑方可視事所派領事等官必須眞正官員不得以商人兼充亦不得兼作貿易易倘各口未設領事官或請別國領事兼代亦不得以商人兼充或即由地方官照現定條約代辨若駐紮朝鮮之美國領事等官辨事不合須知照美國公使彼此意見相同可將批准文憑追回
paragraphs.en: Article 2. Having now established trade and friendship by this treaty, the two countries may exchange envoys with authority to reside in each other's capitals, and may at their pleasure establish consuls and other officers at each other's treaty ports. These officials shall conduct their dealings with local officials in courtesy appropriate to their rank, and the envoys and consuls of the two countries shall enjoy all manner of favours and privileges equal to those of officials of the most-favoured nation. A consul must hold the exequatur of the country in which he resides before he may take up his duties; consuls dispatched must be genuine officials and may not be merchants serving concurrently, nor may they engage in trade. If any port has no consul, a consul of another country may be asked to act for him, but he too may not be a merchant acting concurrently, or else the matter shall be handled by the local official in accordance with the present treaty. If an American consul stationed in Joseon conducts business improperly, the American minister is to be notified, and if the two sides agree, his exequatur may be withdrawn.

paragraphs.orig: 第三款美國船隻在朝鮮在近海面如遇颶風或缺粮食煤水距通商口岸太遠應許其隨處收泊以避颶風購買粮食收理船隻所有經費係由船主自備他方官民應加憐恤援助供其所需如該船主不通商之口潜往貿易拿獲船貨入官如美國船隻在朝鮮海岸破壞朝鮮他方官一經聞知即應飭令將水手先行救護供其粮食等項一面設法保護船隻貨物並行知照領事官俾將水手送回本國幷將船貨撈起一切費用或由船主或由美國認還
paragraphs.en: Article 3. If American vessels, when in the waters near Joseon, meet a typhoon, or lack provisions, coal or water and are too far from a treaty port, they shall be permitted to anchor wherever they are, to shelter from the typhoon, buy provisions and repair the vessel; all expenses are borne by the shipmaster himself, and the local officials and people should show compassion and give assistance, supplying what is needed. If the master secretly goes to a port not open to trade to trade there, the vessel and cargo shall be seized and confiscated. If an American vessel is wrecked on the coast of Joseon, the Joseon local officials, as soon as they hear of it, shall at once give orders to rescue the sailors first and supply them with provisions and the like, and at the same time take steps to protect the vessel and its cargo, and notify the consul so that he may send the sailors home and salvage the vessel and cargo; all the expenses shall be borne either by the shipmaster or by the United States.

paragraphs.orig: 第四款美國民人在朝鮮居住安分守法其性命財産朝鮮地方官應當代爲保護勿許稍有欺凌損毁如有不法之徒欲將美國房屋業産搶劫燒毁者地方如一經領事告知即應派兵彈壓並査拏罪犯按律重辨朝鮮民人如有欺凌美國民人應歸朝鮮官按朝鮮律例懲辨美國民人無論在商船在岸上如有欺凌騷擾損傷朝鮮民人性命財産等事應歸美國領事官或美國所派官員按照美國律例査拏懲辨其在朝鮮國內美國民人如有涉訟應由被告所屬之官員以本國律例審斷原告所屬之國可以派員聽審審官常以禮相待聽審官如欲傳訊査訊分訊證見亦聽其便如以審官所斷爲不公亦許其詳細駁辯大美國與大朝鮮國彼此明定如朝鮮日後改定律例及審案辨法在美國視與本局律例辨法相符即將美國官員在朝鮮審案之權收以後朝鮮境內美國民人即歸地方官管轄
paragraphs.en: Article 4. American citizens residing in Joseon, who live peaceably and keep the law, shall have their lives and property protected by the Joseon local authorities, and no insult or damage shall be permitted. If lawless persons seek to loot or burn American houses and property, the local authorities, once informed by the consul, shall send troops to suppress them, arrest the criminals and punish them severely according to law. If Joseon people insult American citizens, they shall be punished by Joseon officials under Joseon law. If American citizens, whether on merchant vessels or on shore, insult, disturb or injure the lives and property of Joseon people, they shall be arrested and punished by the American consul or by officials dispatched by the United States, according to American law. If American citizens in Joseon become involved in litigation, the case shall be tried by the officials of the country to which the defendant belongs, under that country's laws; the country of the plaintiff may send an official to attend the hearing, and the judge shall always treat him with courtesy; if the attending official wishes to summon, examine or cross-examine witnesses, this too is at his discretion; and if he considers the judge's verdict unjust, he is permitted to argue against it in detail. Great America and Great Joseon expressly agree that if Joseon later revises its laws and its methods of trial, and America finds them in accord with its own laws and methods, the right of American officials in Joseon to try cases shall be withdrawn, and thereafter American citizens within Joseon shall come under the jurisdiction of the local authorities.

paragraphs.orig: 第五款朝鮮國商民並其商船前往美國貿易凡納稅船鈔並一切各費應遵照美國海關章程辨理與征收本國人民及相待最優之國稅鈔不得額外加增美國商民並其商船前往朝鮮貿易進出口貨物均應納稅其收稅之權應由朝鮮自主所有進出口稅項及海關禁防偸漏諸弊悉聽朝鮮政府設立規則先期知會美國官布示商民遵行現擬先訂稅則大略各色進口貨有關民生日用者照估價値百抽稅不得三十至出口土貨槪照値百抽稅不得過五凡進口洋貨除在口岸完納正稅外該項貨物或入內地或在口岸永遠不納別項稅費美國商船進朝鮮口岸須納船鈔每噸銀五錢每船按中歷一季抽一次
paragraphs.en: Article 5. Joseon merchants and their vessels going to America to trade shall, as to all tonnage dues and all other charges, comply with the regulations of the American customs; the duties levied on them shall not be raised beyond those on its own people and on the most-favoured nation. American merchants and their vessels going to Joseon to trade shall pay duty on all goods imported and exported; the right to collect duties belongs to Joseon's own authority. All import and export duties, and customs rules against smuggling and other abuses, shall be set by the Joseon government, which shall first notify the American authorities, who shall make them known to merchants to be observed. For the present a tariff is provisionally drawn up in outline: for goods of all kinds imported that are bound up with the people's daily use, duty shall be levied at a percentage of the assessed value, not to exceed thirty [text defective]; for native goods exported, duty shall in all cases be levied at a percentage of value not exceeding five. For all foreign goods imported, after paying the regular duty at the port, whether the goods go inland or stay at the port, no other tax or charge shall ever be levied. American merchant vessels entering a Joseon port shall pay tonnage dues of five mace of silver per ton, levied once per Chinese season for each vessel.

paragraphs.orig: 第六款朝鮮國商民前往美國各處准其在該處居住賃房買地起蓋棧房任其自便其貿易工作一切所有土産以及製造之物與不違禁之貨均許賣買美國商民前往朝鮮已開口岸准其在該處所定界內居住賃房租地建屋任其自便其貿易工作一切所有土産以及製造之物與不違禁止貨均許賣買惟租地時不得梢油靭逼該地租價悉照朝鮮所定等則完納其出租之地仍歸朝鮮版圖除按此約內所指明歸美國官員應管商民錢産外皆仍歸朝鮮地方官管轄美國商民不得以洋貨運入內地售賣亦不得自入內地採買土貨倂不得以土貨由此口販運彼口違者將貨物入官並將該商交領事官懲辨
paragraphs.en: Article 6. Joseon merchants going to any place in America are permitted to reside there, rent houses, buy land and build warehouses as they please, and to trade and work, and to buy and sell all native produce and manufactured goods and any goods not prohibited. American merchants going to Joseon's open ports are permitted to reside within the limits fixed there, rent houses, rent land and build houses as they please, and to trade and work, and to buy and sell all native produce and manufactured goods and any goods not prohibited. But in renting land they may not coerce or force down the rent, which shall be paid in full according to the rates fixed by Joseon; land so rented remains within Joseon's territory; apart from American officials' control, as specified in this treaty, over the persons and property of American merchants, all remain under the jurisdiction of the Joseon local officials. American merchants may not carry foreign goods into the interior to sell, nor go into the interior to buy native goods, nor ship native goods from one port to another; offenders shall have their goods confiscated and the merchant handed over to the consul for punishment.

paragraphs.orig: 第七款朝鮮國與美國彼此商定朝鮮商民不准販運洋藥入美國通商口岸美國商民亦不准販運洋葯入朝鮮通商口岸並山此口運往彼口亦不准作一切賣買洋藥之貿易所有兩國商民無論僱用本國船別國船及本國船爲別國商民僱用販運洋箹者均山各本國自行永遠禁止査出從重懲罰
paragraphs.en: Article 7. Joseon and America agree that Joseon merchants shall not be allowed to carry opium to the treaty ports of America, and American merchants shall not be allowed to carry opium to the treaty ports of Joseon, nor transport it from one port to another or engage in any trade in opium. Merchants of the two countries, whether they hire ships of their own country or of another, or whether their own ships are hired by merchants of another country, who carry opium shall in all cases be prohibited forever by their own countries, and if discovered shall be severely punished.

paragraphs.orig: 第八款如朝鮮因有事故恐致境內缺食大朝鮮國君主暫禁米粮出口經地方官照知後山美國官員轉飭在各口美國商民一體遵辨惟於己開仁川一港各色米粮槪行禁止運出紅蔘一項朝鮮舊禁出口美國人如有潜買出洋者均査拏入官仍分別懲罰
paragraphs.en: Article 8. If Joseon, owing to some emergency, fears a shortage of food within its borders, the sovereign of Great Joseon may temporarily prohibit the export of rice and grain; after the local officials have given notice, American officials shall instruct American merchants at each port to comply alike. But at the one port of Incheon, already open, the export of all kinds of rice and grain is prohibited generally. Red ginseng is an item long prohibited for export from Joseon; any American who secretly buys it to take abroad shall be arrested, the goods confiscated, and he shall also be punished.

paragraphs.orig: 第九款凡砲位鎗刀火箹鉛丸一切軍器應山朝鮮官自行采辨或美國人奉朝鮮官准買明文方准進口如有私販査貨入官仍分別懲罰
paragraphs.en: Article 9. Cannon, guns, swords, firearms, shot and all other weapons of war shall be purchased by Joseon officials themselves, or may be imported only by Americans who hold a written permit from Joseon officials to purchase; if any are smuggled, the goods shall be seized and the offender punished.

paragraphs.orig: 第十款凡兩國官員商民在彼此通商地方居住均可僱請各色人等勷執分內工藝若朝鮮人遇犯本國例禁或牽涉被控凡在美國商民寓所行棧及商船隱匿者山地方官照知領事官有或准差役自行住拏或山領事派人拏交朝鮮差役美國官民不得稍有庇縱揟留
paragraphs.en: Article 10. Officials and merchants of the two countries residing at each other's treaty places may hire persons of various kinds to assist with their work. If a Joseon person violates his country's prohibitions or is implicated and accused, and hides in the residence, warehouse or vessel of an American merchant, the local officials shall notify the consul, who may either permit officers to go and arrest him, or send men to hand him over to the Joseon officers; American officials and people shall not shelter or detain him.

paragraphs.orig: 第十一款兩國生徒往來學習語言文字律例藝業等事彼此均宜勷助以敦睦誼
paragraphs.en: Article 11. The students of the two countries who go to and from to study languages, writing, law, arts and the like shall be helped by both sides to foster friendship.

paragraphs.orig: 第十二款玆朝鮮國初均立約所訂條欵姑從簡略應遵條約己載者先行辨理其未載者俟五年後兩國官民彼此言語稍通再行議定至通商詳細章程須酌照萬國公法通例公平商訂無有輕重大小之別
paragraphs.en: Article 12. Since this is the first treaty Joseon has made, its articles are provisionally kept brief. What is already recorded in the treaty shall be carried out first; what is not recorded shall be settled after five years, when the officials and people of the two countries have come to understand each other's languages somewhat better. As for detailed trade regulations, they should be fairly settled with reference to the common usage of international law, without distinction of heavy or light, large or small.

paragraphs.orig: 第十三款此均兩國訂立條約與夫日後往來公牘朝鮮專用華文美國亦用華文或用英文必須以華文註明以免岐誤
paragraphs.en: Article 13. In the conclusion of this treaty, and in all official correspondence henceforth, Joseon shall use Chinese only, and America shall also use Chinese, or English with a Chinese annotation, to avoid error.

paragraphs.orig: 第十四款現經兩國議定嗣後大朝鮮國君主有何惠政恩典利益施及他國或其商民無論關涉海而行船通商貿易交往等事爲該國並共商民從來未霑抑爲此條約所無者亦准美國官民、禮均霑惟此種優待他國之利益若入有專條互相酬報者美國官民必將互訂酬報之專條、體遵守方准同霑優待之利益
paragraphs.en: Article 14. It is now agreed between the two countries that if the sovereign of Great Joseon hereafter grants to another country or its merchants any favour, grace or benefit, whether touching navigation, trade, intercourse or the like, which that country and its merchants have not before enjoyed and which is not provided in this treaty, American officials and people shall likewise share it. But where the benefit given to the other country is in return for a special article of reciprocation, American officials and people must likewise agree to a special article of reciprocation and comply with it in full before they may share the favoured benefit.

paragraphs.orig: 以上各欵現經大朝鮮大　美國大臣同在朝鮮仁川府議定繕寫洋華文各三分句法相同先行畫押盖印以昭憑信仍俟兩國御筆批准總以一年爲期在朝鮮仁川府互換然後將此約各欵彼此通諭本國官員商民俾得咸知遵守
paragraphs.en: The above articles have now been agreed upon by the ministers of Great Joseon and Great America together at Incheon in Joseon, and written out in foreign (English) and Chinese texts, three copies each, with identical meaning; they have first signed and sealed them as proof of good faith, and await the ratification of the two countries by the sovereigns' own hand, within one year at the latest, to be exchanged at Incheon in Joseon, whereupon each side will announce the articles to its own officials and people so that all may know and observe them.

paragraphs.orig: 大朝鮮國開國四百九十一年即中國光緖八年四月初六日全權大臣經理統理機務衙門事 申　櫶 印全權副官經理統理機務衙門事 金弘集 印
paragraphs.reading: 대조선국개국사백구십일년즉중국광서팔년사월초육일전권대신경리통리기무아문사 신 헌 인전권부관경리통리기무아문사 김홍집 인
paragraphs.en: The 491st year of the founding of Great Joseon, that is, the 8th year of Guangxu in China, fourth month, sixth day. Plenipotentiary in charge of the Office for Handling State Affairs, Shin Heon [seal]; Deputy Plenipotentiary in charge of the Office for Handling State Affairs, Kim Hong-jip [seal].

paragraphs.orig: 大美國一千八百八十二年五月二十二日全權大臣水師總兵 薛斐爾 印(Signed) R. W. SHUFELDT
